title: Spherical compact sources: Schwarzschild spacetime and relativistic stars
summary: Static spherically symmetric spacetimes and the areal radius; the exterior solution, the Schwarzschild metric and Birkhoff's theorem; the interior mass function and the TOV equations; constant-density stars and the Buchdahl limit; polytropes; perihelion precession and light bending.

objectives.description: Objectives will be finalised when the unit is prepared; the source material is 8.962 Lectures 20–21 (Lecture Guide pages 8–10), Tong Section 1.3 and Carroll Chapter 7.

preparation.description: Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of Lecture 20 (PDF pages 8–9): the static spherically symmetric ansatz, the exterior solution and the Schwarzschild metric.
Read the Lecture Guide's synopsis of the rest of Lecture 20 and Lecture 21 (PDF pages 9–10): mass function, TOV equations, constant-density stars, Buchdahl's theorem, polytropes.
Watch Lectures 20 and 21 (Spherical Compact Sources I and II) from the video gallery (transcripts on each lecture page).
Second account: Tong, General Relativity, Section 1.3 A First Look at the Schwarzschild Metric (geodesics, planetary orbits, precession, light bending), reference-only.
Optional: Carroll, Chapter 7 The Schwarzschild Solution and Black Holes (first half), reference-only.
